'''Travis Lyle Diener''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|iː|n|ər}} {{respell|DEE|nər}};<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/global/intl_player_pronunciation_070426.html |title=NBA.com International NBA Players - Pronunciation Guide |website=www.nba.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070503191308/http://www.nba.com/global/intl_player_pronunciation_070426.html |archive-date=2007-05-03}}</ref>  born March 1, 1982) is an American-Italian former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli Cremona]] in the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He also holds Italian citizenship, and has played for the [[Italian national basketball team|Italian national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2013]].

==Career==
Diener played collegiately at [[Marquette University]], and was a member of the Golden Eagles team that reached the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament Final Four]] in 2003. Diener was one of three future NBA players from that Golden Eagles team; the others were [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Steve Novak]].

Following his [[college basketball|college]] career at Marquette, he was a second-round draft choice (38th overall) of the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]].

Diener made his NBA debut on December 2, 2005, playing 12 minutes and scoring three points in a loss against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200512020MEM.html Orlando Magic at Memphis Grizzlies Box Score]</ref>

On June 19, 2007, the [[Indiana Pacers]] signed Diener (who was a free agent) to a three-year deal reportedly worth $4.86 million.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dienetr01.html <!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On July 6, 2009, Diener exercised his player option to remain with the Pacers for the [[2009-10 NBA season]]. He was waived by Indiana and signed by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in March 2010.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/120/ItemID/1259/Default.aspx|title=Trail Blazers sign Travis Diener|date=March 3, 2010|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers|access-date=March 3, 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125182612/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/120/ItemID/1259/Default.aspx|archive-date=January 25, 2013}}</ref>

In August 2010, he was signed by [[Dinamo Sassari]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].

In May 2013, he acquired Italian citizenship through his wife, who is of Italian descent. This allowed him to join the [[Italian national basketball team]].<ref>[http://www.brewcityball.com/forums/content.php?613-Travis-Diener-Becomes-Italian-Citizen Travis Diener Becomes Italian Citizen]</ref><ref>[http://www.eurobasket2013.org/en/cid_8Xfg3jZMG1QuJnp6pnUWd3.playerID_88066.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2013.roundID_8732.teamID_307.html Travis Diener] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130911233419/http://www.eurobasket2013.org/en/cid_8Xfg3jZMG1QuJnp6pnUWd3.playerID_88066.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2013.roundID_8732.teamID_307.html |date=2013-09-11 }}. FIBA.com.</ref>

In 2014, Diener retired from professional basketball,<ref>{{cite news|title=Travis Diener retires at 32|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/122293/travis-diener-retires-at-32.html|access-date=June 9, 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> after which he became director of player personnel at Marquette University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Travis Diener joins Wojo's staff at Marquette|last= Hunt| first=Michael| url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/262724041.html|access-date=June 12, 2014|newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|date=June 11, 2014}}</ref> His jersey number 12 was retired by Dinamo Sassari.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.lanuovasardegna.it/sport/2014/06/11/news/emanuele-e-travis-diener-dopo-di-loro-nessun-altro-12-1.9405781|title=Emanuele e Travis Diener, dopo di loro nessun altro 12|date=11 June 2014|access-date=9 April 2018|language=it|publisher=Lanuovasardegna.it}}</ref>

In July 2017, Diener came out of retirement to sign with [[Vanoli Cremona]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/basket/2017/07/25/news/travis_diener_a_cremona-171621767/|title=Basket, Travis Diener torna in campo. A Cremona ritrova Drake e Sacchetti|publisher=Repubblica.it|language=it|date=25 July 2017|access-date=6 April 2018}}</ref> He re-signed with the club in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Travis Diener officially re-signs with Vanoli Cremona |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/280504/travis-diener-officially-re-signs-with-vanoli-cremona.html |website=Sportando |access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Diener has played for [[Golden Eagles (TBT)|Golden Eagles]] (a team primarily consisting of Marquette alumni) in [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT), an annual single-elimination winner-take-all tournament. In five games of [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|TBT 2018]], he averaged 8.6 points, 4.2 assists, and shot 43 percent from the field. Golden Eagles reached the semi-finals before falling to the eventual champions, [[Overseas Elite]].  Diener rejoined the Marquette alumni team for the "Championship Weekend" of [[The Basketball Tournament 2019|TBT 2019]], hitting the deciding three-pointer of a semi-final win over Team Hines,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/news/1-golden-eagles-68-1-team-hines-62 |title=#1 Golden Eagles 68, #1 Team Hines 62 |website=thetournament.com |date=August 4, 2019 |access-date=July 14, 2020}}</ref> before Golden Eagles fell to [[Carmen's Crew]] (a team primarily consisting of [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] alumni) in the final. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2020|TBT 2020]], he again joined Golden Eagles for its final contests.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/travis-diener-makes-2020-debut-golden-eagles-win |title=Travis Diener Makes 2020 Debut in Golden Eagles Win |website=thetournament.com |date=July 14, 2020 |access-date=July 14, 2020}}</ref> During the championship game against Sideline Cancer, Diener made one basket, the winning three-pointer that clinched the championship for Golden Eagles, along with the tournament's $1 million prize.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/travis-dieners-only-bucket-game-most-important-one |title=Travis Diener's Only Bucket of the Game is the Most Important One |website=thetournament.com |date=July 14, 2020 |access-date=July 14, 2020}}</ref>
